_ref: Git ref the per-video `test` links point at. Keep on "master"; point it at a branch only while that branch's tests are unmerged, or the links 404.

videos.title: Private accounts, module-side auth
videos.blurb: The same two-client lobby after passwords moved into the database. account is now a private table, so no client can read a verifier — not even the game server, which is why verify_login does the Argon2id work inside the module and returns only a verdict. Hashing also moved off the 64 Hz tick: inline, a 40-login flood froze every player for 1.95 s. Each client still holds its own anonymous identity, visible here as chat attributed correctly to ana and bo.

videos.title: SpacetimeDB lobby and chat
videos.blurb: Two real GPU clients on one database-backed server. Both see the server registry that SpacetimeDB published, and the chat travelling between them never touches the game server — it goes client → database → client. Each client holds its own anonymous identity, bound to its game account by a server-only link_identity reducer.

videos.title: 300 rigid bodies, both first-person views
videos.blurb: alice left, bob right — the same 300 server-simulated rigid bodies, reconstructed independently from delta snapshots over two separate connections. The paired assertion suite (props.rs) puts the worst cross-client disagreement at 0.000 units.

videos.title: Player collision over a lossy link
videos.blurb: Two players walking into each other, jumping on top of each other, through simulated latency, gaussian jitter and packet loss (SOILS_NETSIM). Peer collision is resolved on the server and re-predicted on each client against that tick's recorded peer set — replaying against current peers is what caused permanent rubber-banding before.
